payload.rationale: As of the Q2 2026 results (Aug 10, 2026), Rocket Lab's own target was only delivery of Neutron to the launch pad in Q4 2026, with first-flight hardware assembly, integration and testing still ongoing. For a maiden orbital-class vehicle, pad arrival is typically followed by weeks to months of integrated testing (tanking tests, wet dress rehearsals, static fires) and licensing/range steps before a launch attempt; comparable debuts (Vulcan, New Glenn, Ariane 6, Electron) saw multi-month gaps between pad delivery and first flight. Neutron's schedule has also slipped repeatedly (2024 → 2025 → 2026), so the interested-party Q4 pad target itself carries meaningful slip risk. A launch before Jan 1, 2027 would require early-Q4 pad delivery plus an unusually compressed, trouble-free campaign. The packet notes no confirmed launch and no exact date as of mid-September 2026. Reasons the estimate could be too high: even the pad-delivery target may slip into 2027, and any anomaly in stage testing or static fire would end 2026 chances. Reasons it could be too low: Rocket Lab is an experienced launch operator with strong incentives (contracts, guidance) to fly in 2026, and it may have completed more work after August than the packet shows; a rapid pad campaign or a launch attempt counting regardless of success would raise the odds. Overall, a low probability around 10% seems appropriate.
limitations: Only one company forward-looking statement from Aug 10, 2026 is available; no independent verification of hardware readiness or post-August progress.
No information on regulatory licensing, static-fire completion, or a stated launch date.
Comparisons to other maiden launches are transfer assumptions, not direct evidence about Neutron.
Whether a failed launch attempt counts as a 'launch' under the contract is not specified in the supplied material.
